You are given a JSP scheduling instance.

Problem description:
- There are multiple jobs and multiple machines.
- Each job consists of tasks; each task requires a specific machine and has a processing duration.
- A machine can process at most one task at a time.
- You must assign a start time to every task so that all machine conflicts are avoided.
- Tasks within the same job must follow the given task order (task 0 then task 1 then ...).

Objective:
- Minimize the makespan (the completion time of the last finishing task).

You will receive the instance below:
{{INSTANCE_INPUT}}

Return your schedule using exactly the following JSON format (no extra keys, no explanations):
```json
{
  "solution": [
    {
      "job": <job_id>,
      "tasks": [
        {
          "task": <task_index>,
          "start": <start_time>,
          "machine": <machine_id>,
          "duration": <duration>
        }
      ]
    }
  ]
}
```
Rules:
- Include every job exactly once in the outer list.
- For each job, include all of its tasks exactly once.
- The `machine` and `duration` must match the instance for that job/task.
- Start times must produce a valid schedule (no machine overlap).
- Use identifiers exactly as they appear in the input.
**Do not include explanations or any extra keys.**

As the head chef, plan start times for every dish so that each recipe step uses its assigned kitchen station for its known duration, steps for each dish occur in the specified sequence, no station processes overlapping steps, and the overall schedule finishes all orders as early as possible.

As the project foreman, create a timeline assigning each renovation activity to its designated machine and duration, obey the given sequence of tasks for each room, prevent any machine from running overlapping activities, and aim to complete all rooms in the shortest possible span.

As the dry cleaning manager, schedule the sequence of treatments for every garment on the machines they require for their stated durations, keep the garment procedures in their prescribed order, avoid simultaneous use of the same machine by multiple treatments, and minimize the time until all garments are finished.

As the service manager at the garage, organize start times for each repair step on its required bay or tool for its known length, follow the ordered sequence of operations for each vehicle, ensure no bay or tool handles overlapping operations, and arrange the plan so all vehicles leave as soon as possible.

As the operating room coordinator, slot each surgical phase onto its specified room or equipment for the indicated duration, respect the prescribed sequence of phases for each patient, prevent any room or piece of equipment from hosting overlapping phases, and minimize the completion time for all scheduled procedures.

As the salon owner, plan appointments so every treatment step uses its assigned chair or station for the required time, perform steps for each client in the given order, make sure no station runs overlapping treatments, and schedule to finish all clients as early as feasible.

As the print shop supervisor, assign each print and finishing operation to its designated press or binder for its known processing time, keep the operations for each print job in the specified sequence, prevent any machine from processing overlapping operations, and minimize the time until the entire batch is complete.

As the photo lab lead, timetable each processing step on its assigned machine for its stated duration, follow the required order of steps for each print run, ensure no machine handles overlapping processing steps, and aim to have all prints completed in the least total time.

As the bakery manager, schedule each production step on the equipment it must use for its given duration, keep the steps of each product in the recipe order, avoid overlapping use of any piece of equipment, and plan so that all baked goods are finished as quickly as possible.

As the rendering farm operator, allocate start times for each scene task on its designated server for its expected runtime, honor the fixed sequence of tasks that make up each shot, prevent any server from running overlapping tasks, and minimize the moment when the entire project is rendered.

As the lab coordinator, schedule experiments so each procedural step uses its assigned instrument for its documented duration, carry out steps for each experiment in the prescribed order, avoid overlapping bookings of the same instrument, and minimize the time until all experiments are completed.

As the data center scheduler, plan job start times so each processing stage uses its specified server for the expected duration, maintain the fixed sequence of stages for each batch job, ensure no server executes overlapping stages, and minimize the time when the full workload is completed.

As the post team lead, schedule editing and finishing tasks so each step runs on its assigned suite or station for its known duration, perform steps for each scene in the required order, prevent simultaneous use of the same facility, and minimize the completion time for the whole film.

As the tailor shop manager, organize the flow so each alteration step takes place on its designated machine for its usual duration, follow the established sequence of adjustments for each garment, avoid overlapping use of the same equipment, and arrange the work to finish all pieces as early as possible.

As the landscaping coordinator, plan equipment assignments and start times so each site activity uses its specific machine for its expected duration, keep activities for each project in their specified order, prevent any machine from being scheduled for overlapping activities, and minimize the time until all projects are finished.

As the electronics assembly supervisor, sequence operations so each assembly step is performed on its required station for the given run time, respect the fixed order of steps for each circuit, avoid overlapping assignments on the same station, and minimize the makespan until the full set of boards is assembled.

As the furniture shop foreman, plan start times for cutting, sanding, and finishing steps so each uses its designated tool for its set duration, keep the task order for each piece as specified, ensure no tool is used by overlapping steps, and aim to complete all pieces in the shortest overall span.

As the sorting hub manager, schedule scanning and handling steps so each parcel operation runs on its required equipment for its expected duration, honor the ordered sequence of steps for each parcel, prevent overlapping use of the same equipment, and minimize the time until the entire load is processed.

As the exhibition setup planner, assign start times so each assembly task is performed with its specified lift or tool for its known duration, follow the specified sequence of tasks for each booth, avoid overlapping use of the same lift or tool, and schedule to have all booths ready as early as possible.

Help me plan when each recipe step should use the available appliances so that every meal is ready as early as possible, given that each step takes a specified amount of time, appliances can handle at most a single step at a time, and the steps for each recipe must be performed in the given order.

Schedule the patient pathway so every case is through recovery as soon as possible while respecting that each clinical step lasts a given time, each room can host only one patient activity at a time, and the stages for each patient must occur in the prescribed sequence.

Plan the crew assignments so construction units are completed in the least elapsed time, given each operation on a unit has a fixed time requirement, each piece of heavy equipment can perform only one operation at a time, and the work steps for each unit must be carried out in the established sequence.

global_fields.scenario_description: Total number of customer orders (dishes) the head chef must schedule; determines how many separate recipe sequences must be placed in the timeline.

global_fields.name: nr_machines
global_fields.scenario_description: Total number of distinct kitchen stations (e.g., oven, stove, prep counter) available; each station can handle at most one recipe step at a time.

global_fields.name: jobs
global_fields.scenario_description: Identifiers for each dish/order to be prepared (one identifier per job); each identifier indexes a fixed sequence of recipe steps that must be executed in order.

global_fields.name: machines
global_fields.scenario_description: Identifiers for each kitchen station/resource (one identifier per machine); used to assign which station is required for each recipe step.

job_task_item_fields.name: job_id
job_task_item_fields.scenario_description: Identifier of the dish (which order) this recipe step belongs to; links the step to the dish's ordered sequence of steps.

job_task_item_fields.name: task_id
job_task_item_fields.scenario_description: Index of the step within the dish's recipe sequence (first step = 0 or 1 depending on convention); enforces the required order of execution for that dish.

job_task_item_fields.name: machine_id
job_task_item_fields.scenario_description: Identifier of the specific kitchen station required for this step (e.g., oven_1, stove_2); the step must run on this station and cannot overlap in time with other steps using the same station.

job_task_item_fields.name: duration
job_task_item_fields.scenario_description: Processing time required for this recipe step on its assigned station (in the schedule's time units, e.g., minutes); the station is occupied for this entire duration when the step runs.

global_fields.name: nr_jobs
global_fields.scenario_description: Total number of rooms to renovate (each room is a job consisting of a sequence of activities). Use this to know how many job sequences must be scheduled.

global_fields.name: nr_machines
global_fields.scenario_description: Total number of distinct machines/resources available for the renovation (e.g., painting station, plumbing crew, sanding machine). Each machine can process at most one activity at a time.

global_fields.name: jobs
global_fields.scenario_description: Identifiers for each room/job (e.g., Room1, Kitchen). Each identifier indexes a fixed ordered list of activities that must be performed for that room.

global_fields.name: machines
global_fields.scenario_description: Identifiers for each machine/resource available (e.g., M1, Painter, Electrician). Tasks reference these identifiers to indicate which resource is required.

job_task_item_fields.name: job_id
job_task_item_fields.scenario_description: The room identifier that this specific activity belongs to. Activities with the same room_id must be executed in the given task order for that room.

job_task_item_fields.name: task_id
job_task_item_fields.scenario_description: The position of this activity in the room's ordered checklist (1-based index). Scheduling must respect increasing task_index within each room so steps are not reordered.

job_task_item_fields.name: machine_id
job_task_item_fields.scenario_description: Identifier of the specific machine/resource required to perform this activity. The chosen machine must be free for the entire activity duration (no overlapping activities on the same machine).

job_task_item_fields.name: duration
job_task_item_fields.scenario_description: Processing time required for the activity, expressed in the schedule's time units (e.g., hours). The activity occupies its required_machine_id for this entire duration and is non-preemptive.

global_fields.name: nr_jobs
global_fields.scenario_description: Total number of garments (jobs) to schedule in the dry‑cleaning shop. Each garment corresponds to a job that must go through a fixed series of treatments in order.

global_fields.name: nr_machines
global_fields.scenario_description: Total number of distinct treatment machines available (e.g., washers, presses, steamers). Each machine can process at most one treatment at a time.

global_fields.name: jobs
global_fields.scenario_description: Identifiers for each garment/job (e.g., coat_1, dress_2). These link tasks to the garment whose ordered treatments must be respected.

global_fields.name: machines
global_fields.scenario_description: Identifiers for each physical machine in the shop. Tasks reference these IDs to indicate which machine they must use.

job_task_item_fields.name: job_id
job_task_item_fields.scenario_description: Identifier of the garment this task belongs to; must match one of the garment_ids and ties the task into that garment's ordered treatment sequence.

job_task_item_fields.name: task_id
job_task_item_fields.scenario_description: The ordinal index of this treatment step within the garment's fixed sequence (e.g., first, second). Earlier indices are precedence constraints for later ones and cannot be reordered.

job_task_item_fields.name: machine_id
job_task_item_fields.scenario_description: The identifier of the specific machine required to perform this treatment step. No two tasks may overlap in time on the same required_machine_id.

job_task_item_fields.name: duration
job_task_item_fields.scenario_description: Processing time required for this treatment on its required machine (in the instance's time units). The duration must be scheduled contiguously and contributes to the final makespan.

job_task_item_fields.name: task_id

job_task_item_fields.name: machine_id
job_task_item_fields.scenario_description: Identifier of the specific bay or tool required to perform this step. Matches an entry in 'machines'/'bays' and enforces that no two steps overlap on the same bay/tool.

job_task_item_fields.name: duration

job_task_item_fields.scenario_description: Sequence index of this surgical phase within the patient's required workflow (1 = first phase, 2 = second, etc.). Phases for the same patient must be scheduled in increasing index order.

job_task_item_fields.name: machine_id
